about: Generalisation design G32 (housing_assembly family), dev.json format. Tier 4: a printed guard over a rotating pulley with a rotation clearance, a belt slot, a motor bolt pattern and a locating pilot, judged as interference and clearance checks against reference models and keep-out volumes. L1 ids match benchmarks/generalize/designs/G32/requirements.md, which holds the L2/L3 tree, the reference models, the assumptions and the traceability. Numbers that are not in the owner's words come from requirements.md section 3 and are provisional. Never put any of these numbers in agent logic: they belong in the request text and in the parts catalogue (nema17_motor, gt2_pulley_20t, gt2_belt_6mm, bolt_m3_iso4762).

methods.inspection: read from the design or mesh (counts, sizes, positions, relations)
methods.analysis: computed by Python (connectivity, interference and clearance against reference models, hand calculations)
methods.demonstration: a stand-in object is placed in the design (fits, rests, does not slide)
methods.test: a probe is applied (spin the pulley envelope, run the belt through the slot, drive a bolt along its axis, slide the guard on)

requests.title: NEMA17 pulley belt guard
requests.request: A guard housing over a 20-tooth GT2 pulley (tooth OD 16 mm, flanges 18 mm) on the 5 mm shaft of a NEMA 17 motor (42.3 mm square, M3 holes on a 31 mm square pattern, 22 mm pilot). The pulley hub sits 3 mm above the motor face and the shaft sticks out 24 mm from the face. The guard must clear the pulley and the shaft by 2 mm all around while leaving one slot on one side for the 6 mm GT2 belt, which runs off straight along that side to a second pulley 100 mm away. It is fastened to the motor with M3 bolts in two of the motor's four M3 face holes, and it is printed in PLA on an FDM printer without supports.
requests.request_notes: Added to the plan brief, all from requirements.md section 3: hub 3 mm above the face and the 100 mm belt run (A1, A2); M3 bolts in two of the four holes (A6); the guard locates on the motor pilot (FD2); PLA and FDM (A9).

l1.text: The design shall place the NEMA 17 motor, the GT2 pulley, the belt and the two M3 bolts from the parts catalogue, with the pulley hub 3 mm above the motor face, and shall declare that layout.

The guard shall clear the rotating pulley and the shaft by at least 2 mm all around, on the sides, over the pulley and over the shaft tip (no more than 3 mm radially and 3.5 mm over the shaft tip, so the guard is not oversized), and shall keep at least 0.5 mm from the belt where it wraps the pulley. Take the wrapped belt as a cylinder whose radius is the pulley tooth radius plus the belt thickness minus the belt tooth height (both from the catalogue), 6 mm tall on the pulley's belt plane.

The guard shall have exactly one slot on the belt side that lets both belt runs leave the guard without touching it with at least 0.5 mm clearance to each run (the runs leave tangentially, straight along the slot side, one on each side of the pulley) and is not oversized (no more than 3 mm wider or taller than the two runs together).

The guard shall be fastened by M3 bolts through clearance holes in two of the motor's four M3 face holes, with bolts that engage the motor thread without bottoming and heads that a screwdriver can reach.
The guard shall sit flat on the motor face, locate on the motor's 22 mm pilot with a sliding fit (0.15 to 0.35 mm per side), and stay inside the 42.3 mm square outline of the motor face.
The guard shall be closed on all sides except the belt slot and the two bolt holes, with walls, cap and ears 2 to 4 mm thick (ears up to 5 mm).
The guard shall go on and come off along the shaft axis without touching the pulley or the shaft.
The guard shall be one manifold body that prints on an FDM printer without supports, with at least 40 percent of its plan bounding box in contact with the print bed.
The guard shall be no larger than 45 x 45 x 35 mm.
The design shall be delivered as an STL (assembly pose), the OpenSCAD source, the declared layout and the agent's own clearance report, and that report shall agree with an independent measurement.

beyond_library: catalogue placement of a motor, a pulley, a belt and bolts by datums, with a rotation envelope
belt geometry: two straight runs tangent to the pulley wrap, derived from catalogue numbers
subtraction: a stepped belt slot, two clearance holes, a bore over a pilot
stepped overhang control: 45 degree corbels and ribs so that ears and the slot roof print without supports
interference checks against a rotation envelope, belt envelopes, driver columns and an install sweep
